why: Inserting the fallback made the model avoid splitting noun heads from immediately following post‑nominal modifiers, so cuts that used to fall between head+modifier were instead moved elsewhere (often earlier), producing roughly equal numbers of improvements and degradations and a small net harm concentrated in short/medium pieces (≤5 words). The change therefore traded fixing head+modifier splits for introducing new early cuts that hurt small pieces and enumerations, so overall H_set did not improve.
lesson: A later revision should respect that repairing head+modifier splits by preferring cuts after the modifier can push cuts into other short spans or break enumerations, so such a fallback must not force additional early cuts in ≤5-word pieces.
